hero.h1: Learn the machines Surat runs on.
hero.sub: Karma is an embroidery academy and design lab in Mota Varachha. Eleven techniques — from flat and zardosi to appliqué, 3D, laser, tufting and emCAD design — taught at the machine, with a trainer next to you.
hero.fact4Value: Shared in person at your demo

families.h2: Choose the skill you want to master.
families.sub: Three families. Start with the one that matches the work you want to do — every course is taught on live machines.

sts.h2: Watch a file become a stitch.
sts.sub: One motif in three states: the emCAD file, the path the machine follows, and the finished piece. Every course teaches all three, because knowing only one of them is what keeps an operator an operator.
sts.note1: Outline, control points and colour blocks: the design as it leaves the screen.
sts.note2: Travel order, density and where the needle enters. Quality is decided here, not at the machine.
sts.note3: Satin fill, beadwork and finishing, on real fabric.
sts.hint: Drag the slider, or use the arrow keys
sts.sliderLabel: Reveal the stages, from file to finished piece

how.h2: Learn the complete workflow, not isolated techniques.
how.line: Every course connects design sense, software, materials and machine work, so you understand why a design succeeds, not just which button to press.
how.s1d: Read artwork the way the trade reads it: technique, density, material.
how.s2d: emCAD pathing and machine-ready files, from the first week it's relevant.
how.s3d: Frames, tension, threading: set up like a professional, not a passenger.
how.s4d: Stitch, check, fix, finish. Your hands learn what quality feels like.

visit.firstTitle: What happens on a first visit

firstSteps.t: You walk in, or message first
firstSteps.d: No appointment needed during studio hours. A message just means someone is expecting you.
The free demo is a real session on a real machine, not a tour and a brochure.
We go through the fee and the batch timings. Deciding the same day is not expected.

trainers.h2: You learn from people who still do the work.
trainers.sub: Not lecturers. Working embroiderers and designers who sit at these machines when class is not running.
trainers.p1Value: Every session, on the production machine — not a demo unit kept for classes.
trainers.p2Value: Gujarati and Hindi, with the English terms the trade actually uses.
trainers.p3Value: Seats per batch are limited, so machine time stays personal.
trainers.p4Value: Doubt-clearing with your trainer during studio hours.
trainers.pendingNote: Trainer profiles — real names, real specialities, real portraits — go here once each one is confirmed. We would rather show you nothing than a stand-in.

investment.h2: What it costs, and what that includes.
investment.sub: Fees depend on the course and batch, so we go through the exact number with you at the free demo. Here is what the fee always covers.
included: Machine time in class: you train on the actual production machine, not a demo unit
Thread, needles and practice fabric for classwork
Course notes and the stitch settings we use in production
Your final project piece to keep and show
Certificate on completion, subject to the attendance rule
Doubt-clearing with your trainer during studio hours
investment.notIncludedTitle: Not included, so there are no surprises
notIncluded: Material for large personal projects beyond classwork
emCAD software licence for your own computer
investment.howBody: Come for the free demo, see the machines, and we will tell you the fee for the course and batch you actually want. No obligation, no pressure to decide the same day.
investment.noGateway: There is no online payment on this website. Fees are paid in person at the studio, with a receipt.

pathway.line: The courses connect. Most students start at one machine technique, add emCAD design, and move into production work or a unit of their own.

stages.d: Frames, tension, threading and material — the part that stops your stitches breaking.
Zardosi, 4-beads, sequence, coding or chain and multi. Depth in one before breadth across many.
Make the files the machines run. This is the step that turns an operator into a designer.
Job work, a studio floor, or your own machines and your own clients.

admissionsPage.title: Joining is a conversation and a chair at a machine.
admissionsPage.sub: There is no online payment on this website and no application fee. You come, you sit at a machine for a free demo class, and then you decide.
admissionsPage.asideBody: Fees depend on the course and batch, so we go through the exact number with you at the demo — not before, and never as a deposit taken online.
admissionsPage.stepsSub: Five steps, none of which cost anything until you have decided.

steps.d: WhatsApp is fastest. Walking in during studio hours works just as well.
Sit at the machine, try the technique, meet the trainer. No obligation either way.
We go through the fee, the timing and the seats available for the batch you want.
About two minutes, in Gujarati or English. Guardian details if you are under 18.
Attendance is marked from the first session, because the certificate depends on it.

admissionsPage.batchesSub: Seats per batch are limited, so machine time stays personal. If nothing here fits, WhatsApp us — batches open regularly.
admissionsPage.beforeTitle: The things people check before deciding
admissionsPage.beforeSub: Answered plainly, so you are not chasing a phone call for basics.
admissionsPage.feesBody: Depend on the course and batch. Shared at your demo or on WhatsApp before you decide anything. Paid in person at the studio, with a receipt.
admissionsPage.eligBody: At least 75% attendance, completed practicals, and a finished final project reviewed by your trainer. Every certificate carries a verification QR.
admissionsPage.langBody: Gujarati and Hindi, with the English terms the trade uses — emCAD, machine names, and so on. Written material follows the same mix.
admissionsPage.bringBody: A notebook. Thread, needles and practice fabric for classwork are provided at the studio.
admissionsPage.handbookSub: The rules that actually affect you, rather than a page of policy.
handbook: Attendance is marked every session; certificate eligibility depends on it.
Missed practicals are adjusted within your batch where possible — tell your trainer early.
Machines are a shared responsibility: setup and care are part of the training.
Bring a notebook; materials for practicals are provided at the studio.
Phones on silent during machine time, for safety and focus.
Respect for trainers, students and the space is non-negotiable.
admissionsPage.faqSub: If yours is not here, ask on WhatsApp and a person will reply.
admissionsPage.formNote: Takes about two minutes, in Gujarati or English.

aboutPage.title: A studio that teaches, and a studio that ships.
aboutPage.intro: Karma is one floor in Mota Varachha doing two things with the same machines: training people who want the skill, and developing embroidery for businesses that need the work done. Neither side is a sideline.
aboutPage.twoSidesSub: This is the part most institutes cannot claim: the trainers are not between jobs, they are between orders.
aboutPage.academyBody: Eleven courses across machine embroidery, the modern techniques and emCAD design. Training happens at the machine from the first session, in Gujarati and Hindi, in morning and evening batches.
aboutPage.labBody: Design development, digitizing and production embroidery for garment businesses. The same machines, the same people, on live commercial work — which is why the teaching stays current.
aboutPage.machinesBody: Every technique taught on this floor, named. Swatches stand in for the studio photographs until the shoot happens — we would rather draw the stitch than borrow someone else’s picture of it.
aboutPage.storyTitle: The story, in the owner’s words
aboutPage.storySub: Three things on this page are the owner’s to say, not ours to write. They are marked, and they stay empty until we have them.
aboutPage.storyBody: The founding story goes here, in the owner’s own words: why Karma started, and what “from design screen to finished stitch” looks like on this floor every day.
aboutPage.karmaBody: What the name and the crown stand for, answered by the person who chose them.
aboutPage.trainersNote: Trainer profiles appear here with real names, photos and specialities once each is confirmed. No stand-ins, ever.
aboutPage.numbersNote: Only numbers we can stand behind. Counts come from the published catalogue; anything about students or ratings stays off this page until the owner has verified it in writing.

storiesPage.title: What changed after the course?
storiesPage.sub: Named outcomes, published with consent: businesses started, jobs landed, rates raised.
storiesPage.consentBody: Every story here is shared with the student’s permission and verified by the studio before it goes up. Unverified entries stay marked as samples.
